entries.reason: This paper presents a novel method for reconstructing molecular energy levels directly from raw, unassigned transition frequencies, using graph theory alone with no model and no prior assignment, which has the potential to revolutionize the field of spectroscopy.
entries.title: Unlocking Molecular Energy Levels Without a Model
entries.paragraph: Researchers have developed a new method to reconstruct molecular energy levels directly from raw, unassigned transition frequencies. This approach uses graph theory to assemble an energy-level network at kilohertz precision, without requiring a Hamiltonian model or prior assignment. The method was applied to the water absorption spectrum, resulting in 158 energy levels that are mostly two orders of magnitude more precise than the corresponding literature values.

entries.reason: This study provides a comprehensive investigation of the electronic properties of phenacene thin films, including ionization energies, electron affinities, band gaps, exciton binding energies, and polarization energies, which are crucial for understanding their potential applications in organic electronics and superconductivity.
entries.title: Quantifying Electronic Properties of Phenacene Thin Films
entries.paragraph: Scientists have determined the ionization energies, electron affinities, band gaps, exciton binding energies, and polarization energies of orientation-controlled thin films of picene, [6]-phenacene, and [7]-phenacene. The results show that these properties depend only weakly on molecular size, but exhibit large orientation-dependent shifts. The band gaps and exciton binding energies remain nearly independent of molecular size and orientation.

entries.reason: This paper presents a novel first-principles approach augmented with regularized regression that identifies spin-phonon relaxation pathways in molecular qubits, which has the potential to improve the design of molecular qubits and enhance their coherence time.
entries.title: Unraveling Spin-Phonon Relaxation Pathways in Molecular Qubits
entries.paragraph: Researchers have developed an alternative first-principles approach to identify spin-phonon relaxation pathways in molecular qubits. This method uses regularized regression to automate the process without ad hoc mode selection. Applied to Cu porphyrins spin-1/2 molecular qubits, the method successfully reproduces experimental trends in relaxation times and predicts the curvature in the relaxation-vs-temperature profile.

entries.reason: This study presents a novel method for resolving intrinsic surfactant adsorption kinetics using geometry-controlled dynamic tensiometry, which has the potential to improve our understanding of surfactant behavior at interfaces and enhance the design of surfactant-based systems.
entries.title: Measuring Surfactant Adsorption Kinetics with Precision
entries.paragraph: Scientists have developed a microfluidic EDGE tensiometer to measure dynamic interfacial tension with high precision. By combining equilibrium and diffusion measurements, they were able to determine the intrinsic adsorption rate constant of nonionic surfactant C$_{10}$E$_{8}$ and SDS. The results show that the model predicts dynamic interfacial tension beyond the geometry and conditions used to determine them.

entries.reason: This paper presents a novel wave function-based machine learning interelectronic representation, which has the potential to improve the accuracy and efficiency of molecular modeling and computational chemistry simulations.
entries.title: A Machine Learning Model for Electronic Structure
entries.paragraph: Researchers have developed a wave function-based machine learning model called OrbGNN, which represents a molecule's orbital landscape and electron correlation patterns. The model is evaluated for the dissociation of nitrogen and for a larger dataset of diatomic molecules. Finally, the OrbGNN model is applied to a set of octahedral iron(II) complexes to predict spin-state energy gaps.
